title: Introduce compatibility shims and OpenSSL 3 migration for auth dependencies
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Technical work to migrate platform build/runtime to OpenSSL 3.x, upgrade JWT/OAuth and SAML libraries across services, and add lightweight compatibility shims so rolling upgrades are non-disruptive. This ticket covers the cross-repo compatibility adapters, CI/Canary gating, migration runbook, and post-upgrade verification. Goal: remove our remaining OpenSSL 1.1 runtime surface, eliminate a CVE risk vector in node-jwt libraries, and ensure SAML assertions continue to validate during staged rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All services pass unit+integration tests against OpenSSL 3.1 and upgraded auth libs in CI. 2) Compatibility shim library available with feature flag to enable/disable per-service. 3) Canary rollout executed in staging and two production regions with telemetry showing no validation failures for SSO flows. 4) Rollback paths validated and documented in runbook.
work_items: Audit every service that links libssl or depends on node-jose / python-jose / go-jwt and mark upgrade priority
Implement compatibility shims for signature verification discrepancies (RSA-PSS defaults, digest aliasing)
Update build images and package manifests to OpenSSL 3.1 and rebuilt native modules
Upgrade passport-saml / ruby-saml adaptors and node-jwt libraries to latest secure versions
Add CI matrix job to run auth integration tests against old and new crypto stacks
Create canary rollout policy and monitoring dashboard for SSO success-rate and token validation latency
Document rollback and mitigation steps in Confluence runbook
decisions: Use a compatibility shim approach rather than simultaneous universal upgrade to reduce blast radius
Prefer OpenSSL 3.1 runtime (vs BoringSSL) for compatibility with existing baked images and vendor support
Add feature flags at service config layer to flip shim behavior per-deployment during canary
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: signature validation semantics change (RSA-PSS vs PKCS#1 v1.5). Mitigation: shim normalizes verification parameters and unit-tests real SAML assertions from partners.
Risk: native module rebuilds fail on some builder images. Mitigation: add reproducible builder image and cross-compile matrix in CI; keep old images available for rollback.
Risk: intermittent SSO failures visible to customers. Mitigation: gradual canary with automated rollback if SSO success_rate drops >0.5% over 5 minutes.
Risk: performance regression in token verification. Mitigation: measure P95 verification latency and cap batch size for synchronous flows; enable caching of parsed keys.
